bills.title: Veterinary Medicine: Registered Veterinary Nurse Title Protection Act
bills.last_action: Referred to Committee on Business and Professions
bills.summary_ai: This bill would establish title protection for the designation 'Registered Veterinary Nurse,' restricting use of the title to credentialed individuals who have passed the VTNE and hold an active California RVT license. The bill also increases penalties for unlicensed use of protected veterinary titles.

bills.title: Relating to the scope of practice of veterinary professional associates
bills.last_action: Passed House Committee on Licensing & Administrative Procedures
bills.summary_ai: This bill expands the scope of practice for Veterinary Professional Associates (VPAs) in Texas, allowing them to perform additional diagnostic and therapeutic procedures under indirect veterinarian supervision. It also establishes a formal VPA licensure pathway within the Texas State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners.

bills.title: Establishes licensure requirements for veterinary technicians in New York State
bills.summary_ai: This bill would create a mandatory licensure framework for veterinary technicians in New York, requiring passage of the VTNE and completion of an accredited veterinary technology program. Currently NY does not mandate state licensure for vet techs; this bill would align NY with the majority of other states.

bills.title: Veterinary Technician Supervision Ratio Reform
bills.summary_ai: This bill amends Florida Statutes to modify the allowable supervision ratio for licensed veterinary technicians from 1:1 to 1:3 (one veterinarian supervising up to three LVTs simultaneously), consistent with national standards. The bill also clarifies the definition of 'direct supervision' versus 'indirect supervision' for specific procedures.

bills.title: Concerning continuing education requirements for credentialed veterinary technicians
bills.summary_ai: Now law: requires Colorado CVTs to complete 20 hours of continuing education every two years for license renewal, including at least 2 hours in veterinary law and ethics. Previously CO had no mandatory CE for vet techs. Effective January 1, 2027.

bills.title: Practice of Veterinary Technology Amendments
bills.summary_ai: This bill would authorize credentialed veterinary technicians in Ohio to perform dental radiographs, place IV catheters, and administer controlled substances under indirect veterinarian supervision. It also proposes eliminating the requirement for veterinarians to physically co-sign technician treatment notes.

bills.title: Expanding veterinary technician specialist recognition in Washington
bills.summary_ai: This bill formally recognizes Veterinary Technician Specialists (VTS) as a distinct credentialed designation in Washington state law, entitling them to perform specialist-level procedures within their VTS academy's defined scope without additional per-procedure veterinarian authorization.

bills.title: Veterinary assistant registration program establishment
bills.summary_ai: Would create a voluntary registration program for veterinary assistants in Minnesota through the Board of Veterinary Medicine, establishing minimum training standards, a competency examination, and a protected 'Registered Veterinary Assistant' title. Registration would not be mandatory but would provide pathway for career advancement.

bills.title: Interstate Compact for Veterinary Technician Licensure
bills.last_action: Referred to House Professional Licensure Committee
bills.summary_ai: Pennsylvania seeks to join a proposed interstate compact allowing LVTs and RVTs licensed in member states to practice in Pennsylvania via endorsement without a separate PA licensure examination. Reciprocity provisions would also benefit Pennsylvania credentialed technicians seeking multi-state practice.

bills.title: Veterinary Nursing Practice Act
bills.summary_ai: This sweeping bill would create the Illinois Veterinary Nursing Practice Act, introducing a two-tier licensure system distinguishing Veterinary Nurses (4-year degree, expanded scope) from Veterinary Technicians (2-year degree, current scope). Both titles would receive legal title protection under the new Act.

bills.title: Veterinary technician: VTNE examination waiver for military spouses
bills.summary_ai: Signed into law: allows military spouses who are credentialed veterinary technicians in another state to obtain an Arizona license by endorsement without re-taking the VTNE, provided they have held their license in good standing for at least 12 months. Effective immediately.

bills.title: Failed: Expanded delegation authority to veterinary assistants
bills.summary_ai: This bill would have allowed veterinarians to delegate vaccine administration, blood draws, and routine medication dispensing to unlicensed veterinary assistants without credentialed technician oversight. The bill failed in committee following opposition from Georgia's veterinary technician community and the Georgia VMA.

board_minutes.summary_ai: The board discussed the proposed 'Registered Veterinary Nurse' title protection bill, with staff presenting an analysis of implementation requirements. The board voted 7-2 to submit a formal letter of support to the Assembly Committee on Business and Professions.

board_minutes.board_name: Texas State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners
board_minutes.summary_ai: The board reviewed proposed rule amendments to Chapter 573 (Veterinary Professional Associates), including updated supervision requirements and expanded task delegation authority. A stakeholder comment period was opened through May 8, 2026.

Board approved updated Rule 61G18-15.002 clarifying that LVTs may perform dental cleanings under indirect supervision when the veterinarian remains on premises. The board also reviewed two disciplinary cases involving unlicensed practice as a veterinary technician.

board_minutes.board_name: New York State Board for Veterinary Medicine
board_minutes.summary_ai: The board reviewed SB 7123 (veterinary technician licensure) and voted to support its passage. Staff presented data showing NY is one of only two remaining states without mandatory vet tech licensure. The board approved guidance for practitioners on current credentialing expectations pending legislation.

board_minutes.board_name: Colorado State Board of Veterinary Medicine
board_minutes.summary_ai: Board finalized implementation guidance for HB 1432 (CVT continuing education requirements), specifying approved CE providers and acceptable subject categories. The board also heard public comment on a petition requesting VTS recognition in Colorado regulation.

Board staff presented analysis of SB 312 (expanded vet tech scope) for board review and comment. The board discussed the proposed authorization for CVTs to place IV catheters under indirect supervision, with members requesting additional data on patient safety outcomes from states with similar rules.

The board reviewed and approved proposed training standards for the voluntary veterinary assistant registration program under HF 2201. Discussion centered on whether the NAVTA Approved Veterinary Assistant (AVA) credential should be accepted in lieu of the proposed state examination.

board_minutes.board_name: Washington State Veterinary Board of Governors
board_minutes.summary_ai: Board received testimony on SB 5678 regarding VTS recognition. Several Washington-licensed VTS credentialed technicians testified about current regulatory gaps. Board voted to formally endorse the legislation and submitted written comments to the Senate Labor & Commerce Committee.
